plan.title: BLOCKER: bug(toolchain): consumer check hard-requires pnpm when packageManager pins npm

narratives.Description: BLOCKER: bug(toolchain): consumer check hard-requires pnpm when packageManager pins npm
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`deft toolchain:check --consumer` hard-requires `pnpm` even when the consumer repository explicitly pins npm through `package.json#packageManager`. Under Corepack, the pnpm shim correctly refuses to run in that npm-pinned repository, and Deft reports pnpm as missing.

The check therefore contradicts the consumer's declared package-manager contract, and the remediation it prints cannot succeed without changing the project.

## Reproduction

Consumer `package.json`:

```json
{
  "packageManager": "npm@11.16.0",
  "devDependencies": {
    "@deftai/directive": "0.105.0"
  }
}
```

`pnpm --version` in that directory, via Corepack:

```text
This project is configured to use npm because .../package.json has a "packageManager" field
```

`deft toolchain:check --consumer`:

```text
pnpm: FAILED (exit 1)
Missing tools: pnpm
Node.js and pnpm are required for TS-backed deft gates.
```

The same pnpm shim works outside the npm-pinned repository and reports 11.8.0.

## Root cause

`CONSUMER_TOOLS` in `packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts` hard-codes `pnpm --version`. It does not inspect `packageManager`, a lockfile, or the manager Corepack has selected.

Corepack's refusal is **correct behaviour**, not an error to route around. Any fix that shells out to pnpm anyway, or runs `corepack enable`, would be worse than the bug.

## The engine does not need pnpm from a consumer -- verified

This was the open question and it is now settled, 3/3 on the round-1 panel (synthesis 5434122672), and it makes the remedy small.

Deft's TS-backed gates have not required pnpm from an npm consumer since #3324. `tasks/engine-pm-run.cjs` is the only pnpm caller; it is reachable only through `_ts-build`, which is gated by `isBuildableSource` and is a no-op on any deposit. Confirmed independently by composition: `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` contains no suite gate, and every entry is CLI-dispatchable through node.

**The former acceptance criterion "internal engine package-manager requirements are isolated from the consumer package manager" has been struck.** It describes an invariant that already holds. It is not deferred and should not be built.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The consumer check resolves the manager from the **project root** and probes that manager there
- [ ] `package.json#packageManager` is **authoritative**; a conflicting `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` is **rejected**, not silently honoured
- [ ] Both remediation surfaces name the selected manager -- selection and remediation ship together, because the reporter's complaint was that the remediation could not succeed
- [ ] Windows shim paths containing `%` resolve correctly
- [ ] npm-pinned and pnpm-pinned consumer fixtures both have deterministic supported behaviour
- [ ] Corepack manager-mismatch behaviour has regression coverage
- [ ] At least one **consumer-path** invocation of `toolchain-check --consumer` runs in CI, not only in-repo unit tests
- [ ] macOS, Linux, and Windows shim behaviour is covered
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

## Defects found in the round-1 implementation (PR #3784)

Recorded here because they are properties of the fix, not of the PR alone, and a re-implementation must avoid them.

**Override precedence inverts the contract.** `resolveProjectPackageManager` returns on `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` before reading `package.json`:

```208:220:packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.ts
  const override = env.DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER;
  if (typeof override === "string" && override.trim() !== "") {
    return resolvePackageManager({ env });
  }
```

A consumer pinning npm with that variable set to pnpm gets pnpm probed, Corepack refuses, and this issue's exact failure returns -- with the diagnostic now attributing the choice to an override rather than to the declaration. `detectPackageManager` is override-first as well, so both entry points carry it.

**Windows percent handling.** `quoteWindowsCommandPath` doubles `%`. Measured: `cmd.exe` does not collapse `%%` on a command line, and doubling does not prevent variable expansion. A shim path containing `%` reports the manager missing -- the same false-negative class this issue exists to eliminate.

**Consumer-path verification is absent.** The CI addition is one in-repo vitest step. No workflow or release-e2e path invokes `toolchain-check --consumer`, and `verify:consumer-check-contract` governs include wiring rather than manager selection. For a defect found by a consumer against a published release, that gap is load-bearing. The existing Windows consumer-deposit fixture job already has the machinery and needs one added invocation, not a new harness.

## Out of scope

- The getting-started documentation rewrite and the `task` removal carried in PR #3784. Neither belongs to this issue.
- Changing Corepack behaviour or enabling Corepack on a consumer's behalf.
- Anything about the framework repository's own package manager.

## Environment (as reported)

`@deftai/directive` 0.105.0, engine 0.105.0, Node 24.18.0, npm 11.16.0, Corepack 0.35.0, available pnpm shim 11.8.0, macOS, zsh.

## Provenance

Filed by @dbcall2 from a live consumer install. The reproduction is the reporter's; the parent has **no npm-pinned consumer fixture** on its machine and did not re-run it. Everything under "the engine does not need pnpm" and "defects found" was derived from source by the round-1 panel and re-verified by the parent at `e2b62217`.

Refs #2022, #2761, #2765, #3324, #2611.

## Triage

mechanism-shaped: true

design-critique: warranted, and unusually this arc has an implementation to critique as well as a design. PR #3784 already implements a fix (22 files, +1819/-111) at Greptile 5/5, rebased onto current master as `a59e7d4c`. It is **not merged and will not be merged before this arc completes.**

refutation-target: the consumer check hard-requires `pnpm` regardless of the consumer's declared package manager, and honoring `package.json#packageManager` in the consumer check is the correct fix.

## Why the target may not hold

The reproduction is clean and I do not doubt it. What I doubt is that the second half follows from the first.

Acceptance criterion 5 says "internal engine package-manager requirements are isolated from the consumer package manager." That is the load-bearing item, and it is doing different work from the other five. If Deft's TS-backed gates genuinely need pnpm to run, then honoring the declared manager does not let an npm consumer run those gates -- it changes the failure from "pnpm: FAILED" to a later, less legible one. The consumer would pass the toolchain check and then fail at the thing the check exists to predict.

Conversely, if the engine does **not** need pnpm from the consumer's side, then `CONSUMER_TOOLS` requiring it is a straightforward mistake and the remedy is small.

Those are materially different issues with different sizes, and the body does not settle which one this is.

## Audit markers

- `audit:engine-need` -- **Do the TS-backed gates actually require pnpm when invoked from an npm consumer?** Determine this from source, not from the task description. If they do, AC5 is the whole issue and the other five criteria are cosmetic. If they do not, AC5 is a no-op and should be struck. This single question sets the size of the work.

- `audit:implementation` -- PR #3784 exists. Read the diff and judge it against the criteria, not just the issue text. Does it select the declared manager, or does it merely stop requiring pnpm? Does it verify the selected manager actually works, or only that it is named? Three SLizard P2s were raised and answered by the author -- newline sanitisation on interpolated diagnostics, a hardcoded Windows path in a test, and Windows shim quoting. **Verify those dismissals independently rather than accepting them**, the way the #3775 fp claim was checked.

- `audit:consumer-verify` -- This defect was reported by a consumer, on macOS, against a published release. Establish whether the fix is verifiable from a consumer's position or only inside this repository. The framework has a consumer kit (#2611) and a consumer-check contract gate. A fix for a consumer-only failure that can only be exercised in-repo has not been demonstrated.

- `audit:scope` -- Six acceptance criteria spanning manager selection, Corepack mismatch coverage, remediation text, engine isolation, and three operating systems. Determine the minimal correct change and whether AC5 is separable. If AC5 is the real issue, the rest may belong behind it rather than beside it.

## Sequencing note

I rebased #3784 onto current master twice tonight -- once to clear a CHANGELOG conflict, once after master moved -- so its current head is mine, not the author's. Its merge gate is presently failing on `a59e7d4c` and I have not yet diagnosed whether that is a real failure or more inherited state. Critics should treat the PR's green/red status as unsettled and judge the diff on its merits.

## Provenance

Issue filed by @dbcall2 from a live consumer install: `@deftai/directive` 0.105.0, Node 24.18.0, npm 11.16.0, Corepack 0.35.0, macOS. The parent has **not** reproduced it -- there is no npm-pinned consumer fixture on this machine -- so the reproduction is inherited and should be re-derived from source rather than trusted.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-27T03:44:58Z)

model: cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast

input-ceiling: 5434075404 (inclusive). Later thread comments are disclosed as existing and excluded from this critique, including 5434077231.

refutation-target: the consumer check hard-requires `pnpm` regardless of the consumer's declared package manager, and honoring `package.json#packageManager` in the consumer check is the correct fix.

charter: presumption-refutation. I tried to break both halves from source. The target survives.

## Verdict

**SURVIVED.** Master `CONSUMER_TOOLS` does hard-require `pnpm --version` and does not inspect `packageManager`, a lockfile, or Corepack. Honoring the declared manager and verifying that manager at the project root is the correct fix. Acceptance criterion 5 is already true on today's engine path and is not the size of this issue.

**PR #3784 (`a59e7d4c`) should not merge as the closer of all six criteria.** The selection-and-verify core is the right shape. AC5 should be struck from the close set. Consumer-position proof is still missing. Unrelated getting-started publication-claim edits should leave this PR.

## Existing mechanisms (inventory)

- `detectPackageManager` already encodes env → `packageManager` → `pnpm-lock.yaml` → user-agent → npm (`packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.ts:48-78`). Toolchain check never calls it.
- Consumer deposits already force the global CLI and a no-op build (`tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:153-161`, `tasks/engine.yml:50-57`, `tasks/engine.yml:62`).
- `engine-pm-run.cjs` runs scripts against `DEFT_ROOT`, not the consumer cwd, and requires `pnpm@<semver>` only when that *framework* `package.json` sets a pin (`tasks/engine-pm-run.cjs:32-57`, `:162-164`).
- Session preflight already has a separate PATH probe that still names `pnpm` (`packages/core/src/session/toolchain-preflight.ts:28`, `:106-110`).
- `verify:consumer-check-contract` checks Taskfile composition (`content/docs/consumer-check-contract.md:10-16`). It does not exercise package-manager selection.
- #2611 is the consumer *issue-label* kit, not a consumer runtime fixture.

## Injection / swarm lens

`package.json#packageManager` is untrusted repo-controlled text at an execution boundary. The PR fail-closes instruction-shaped values (`pnpm@11.8.0; touch …`) before any spawn and maps a closed `npm | pnpm` union onto fixed `["<manager>", "--version"]` argv. Raw field text is not interpolated into a command. Windows PATH resolution prefers an absolute candidate so `cmd.exe` cannot pick a repo-local shim. No authority, identity, worktree, or A2A change. Residual injection risk is low.

---

## 1. Engine isolation is already true — AC5 is not the issue

class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** A consumer deposit is not a buildable source. `isBuildableSource` returns false when the deposit marker / `.deft/core` path / content-package name is present (`tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:153-161`). `_ts-build` is then a no-op (`tasks/engine.yml:50-57`). `engine:invoke` runs the global `deft` / `directive` binary installed with `npm i -g @deftai/directive` (`tasks/engine.yml:161-168`). Runtime/session verbs are forbidden from triggering `engine:_ts-build` / pnpm (`tasks/engine.yml:62`). Consumer `check` has no `ts:check-lane` (`packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:128-145`). `packages/cli/src` has no `pnpm` spawn. `engine-pm-run.cjs` is a framework-source script runner; its cwd is `DEFT_ROOT`.

**Failure mode if we treat AC5 as new work.** This issue becomes an engine rewrite. The reporter's failure is `pnpm: FAILED` on `toolchain:check --consumer`, not a later TS gate invoking pnpm from the consumer cwd. Expanding AC5 would hide a one-line contract mismatch behind a second architecture.

**Disposition.** Strike AC5 as a *new* requirement. Keep a non-regression note: do not teach `engine-pm-run` to honor the *consumer* pin. The xBRIEF at `a59e7d4c` points AC5 at `package-manager.test.ts`. That tests the new resolver, not engine isolation. That pointer does not satisfy AC5 as written.

**audit:engine-need.** TS-backed gates do **not** require pnpm when invoked from an npm consumer. `CONSUMER_TOOLS` requiring pnpm is a plain mistake. The other five criteria are the real issue. They are small.

---

## 2. First half of the target is measured, not inherited

class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Master `CONSUMER_TOOLS` is git, gh, node, pnpm, task (`packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:19-25`). Selection is `options.consumer ? CONSUMER_TOOLS : MAINTAINER_TOOLS` (`:101`). No `packageManager` read, no lockfile, no Corepack query. Failed pnpm always appends `NODE_RUNTIME_REMEDIATION` (`packages/core/src/verify-env/node-runtime.ts:3-13`), which tells the consumer to `corepack prepare pnpm@latest --activate`. That is the reported loop: Corepack correctly refuses pnpm in an npm-pinned tree; Deft then tells the operator to enable pnpm.

The comment on `CONSUMER_TOOLS` already says "Consumer npm-deposit toolchain (#2022 Phase 3)" while listing pnpm. The contradiction is in the current source, not only in the issue prose.

**Failure mode.** A critic who trusted the unreproduced report could have called this a docs-only mismatch. It is not.

**Disposition.** Keep the first half of the target. The parent's `CONSUMER_TOOLS` framing holds.

---

## 3. Honoring the declared manager is the correct small fix

class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Because the engine does not invoke the consumer's package manager, the check's job is to stop lying. It must select the declared manager, run that manager's `--version` at the project root (so Corepack's refusal remains visible when the *selected* manager is wrong), and name that manager in remediation. It must not spawn the unselected manager.

PR #3784 does that, not merely "stop requiring pnpm":

- `resolveProjectPackageManager` reads `package.json#packageManager`, then lockfile / user-agent / default (`package-manager.ts` patch on `a59e7d4c`).
- Consumer tools become shared git/gh/node plus `PACKAGE_MANAGER_TOOLS[packageManager]`.
- The probe cwd is `projectRoot` (`toolchain-check.ts` patch; `tasks/toolchain.yml` adds `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"`).
- Tests assert an npm-pinned fixture never sees `pnpm` on the runner.
- Instruction-shaped pins fail before spawn.
- Remediation splits npm vs pnpm (`node-runtime.ts` patch; `named-cause.ts` patch).

Corepack refusal is treated as correct behavior. The fix does not shell out to pnpm in an npm-pinned tree and does not bypass Corepack.

**Failure mode of the rejected alternative.** Deleting the pnpm row and probing nothing would silence the reporter and would not verify that the declared manager actually runs. Steelmanning that alternative: if no later consumer gate invokes the project manager, a presence check is theater. What flips it: Corepack still enforces the pin on any later `pnpm` the operator or an agent types, and today's remediation *instructs* that command. Selecting and verifying the declared manager stops both the false fail and the false remedy.

**Disposition.** Bind the second half of the target. Judge the PR against select-and-verify, not against "drop pnpm."

**audit:implementation.** The PR selects the declared manager and verifies it with a real `--version` probe at the project root. It does not merely stop requiring pnpm.

---

## 4. SLizard P2s — independent check

class: footnote

**Newline sanitisation (`toolchain-check.ts` ~231 / ~269).** `sanitizeSingleLineDiagnostic` maps Unicode Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp (including `\n`) to spaces, collapses whitespace, and bounds to 240 code points. Resolver error messages go through that helper before interpolation. Failed-probe text goes through `pythonSplitlines` plus the same helper (`firstSafeDiagnostic`). The author's replies hold. The original P2s were real on the first interpolation shape and are closed on `a59e7d4c`.

**Hardcoded `C:\\trusted\\npm.CMD` in a test.** The test injects `platform: "win32"`, `exists`, and `execFileSync`. Those strings are logical inputs to seams, not host filesystem access. Dismissal holds.

**Windows shim quoting (~:143).** The original finding was real: libuv re-escapes, `cmd /s` strips the outer pair, a spaced `.cmd` path breaks. The repair uses a fixed `SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe`, an outer-quoted `/c` command that already contains an inner-quoted absolute shim, and `windowsVerbatimArguments: true`. Shape matches Node's CMD plan. This was a fix, not a dismissal. Independent reading agrees.

---

## 5. The fix is not demonstrated from a consumer's position

class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Literal AC on the xBRIEF is an in-repo Vitest command over six test files. Those tests inject runners. The "does not invoke a Corepack-rejected pnpm shim" case never execs Corepack; it only asserts the mock is not called with `pnpm`. Windows CI adds `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.test.ts` — still in-repo.

`verify:consumer-check-contract` does not speak this contract. #2611 does not. `greenfield-python-free-smoke` still fail-closes if neither pnpm nor Corepack is on PATH (`packages/core/src/release-e2e/greenfield-python-free-smoke.ts:122-124`) and is a maintainer pack/init smoke, not an npm-pinned consumer install of a published tarball.

The defect was found on published 0.105.0, macOS, live Corepack. That path is not in the PR.

**Failure mode.** In-repo mocks can go green while a consumer on Corepack 0.35 + `packageManager: "npm@…"` still fails a missed cwd, a missed env, or a published-pack drift.

**Disposition.** Do not treat #3610 as demonstrated until one of: (a) a live Corepack cwd fixture that really execs `pnpm --version` / `npm --version` against temp `package.json` pins, or (b) a pack-and-install consumer smoke, or (c) an explicit residual that consumer-position proof is post-release. Option (a) is the cheapest and can stay in this repo.

**audit:consumer-verify.** Verifiable from a consumer's position *after* a release by re-running `deft toolchain:check --consumer` in the reporter's tree. Not demonstrated by this PR. The in-repo suite does not substitute.

---

## 6. Scope: five small criteria, one already-true isolation clause, extra blast in the PR

class: sharpens-framing

**Minimal correct change.**

1. Stop hard-coding `pnpm` on the consumer list.
2. Select `npm | pnpm` from the existing precedence, fail-closed on unsupported / instruction-shaped values.
3. Probe the selected manager at the consumer project root.
4. Name that manager in remediation (`node-runtime` + `named-cause`).
5. Companion: session preflight must probe the same manager, not `which("pnpm")`, or an npm consumer with no pnpm shim fails the *next* gate. The reporter had a pnpm shim (11.8.0), so preflight `which` would have passed them; consumers without any pnpm install would not.

AC5 is separable and already true. The OS matrix is not the reporter's bug (macOS/Corepack). Windows `.cmd` / PATHEXT work is justified only because the new npm probe would otherwise regress Windows npm consumers once the old `shell: true` ENOENT fallback is removed. That is real, but it is a consequence of the runner rewrite, not of honoring `packageManager`.

**PR extras that do not belong in the close set.**

- Removing `task` from `CONSUMER_TOOLS` aligns with #3335 CLI-dispatch, not with #3610.
- `inferConsumerDeposit` equal-roots repair is load-bearing for preflight. Master `isFrameworkSourceContext` returns true whenever the two roots are equal (`packages/core/src/check/context.ts:38-39`). Old preflight therefore classified a same-root consumer as maintainer and kept probing pnpm. Keep that repair; do not bury it as incidental.
- `content/docs/getting-started.md` deletes the "#1909 not yet published" banner and declares npm canonical since v0.55.1. The reporter used published 0.105.0, so the old banner is stale, but that edit is not this bug.
- Default when no field and no lockfile becomes **npm** (`resolvePackageManager` → `DEFAULT_PACKAGE_MANAGER`). Master consumer check always probed pnpm. A pnpm repo with neither `packageManager` nor `pnpm-lock.yaml`, invoked via global `deft` (no user-agent), flips from "must have pnpm" to "must have npm." Declared pnpm consumers (`packageManager: "pnpm@…"` or lockfile) keep a `pnpm --version` probe. Preserve that class exactly; document the undeclared default.

**Disposition.** Bind criteria 1–4 as the issue. Strike AC5 as new work. Keep AC6 as Windows-runner coverage for the new npm probe, not as a third-OS reproduction of the reporter. Do not close #3610 from the getting-started publication rewrite.

**audit:scope.** Minimal change is select + cwd-verify + remediation + preflight companion. AC5 is separable and already satisfied. Everything else is either that companion or blast.

---

## 7. Regression to pnpm consumers

class: footnote

Declared pnpm consumers still run `pnpm --version` at the project root. Corepack will accept. Maintainer `MAINTAINER_TOOLS` still includes pnpm. Framework `engine-pm-run` is untouched. The majority path that pins or lockfiles pnpm is preserved.

Risk is the undeclared-pnpm default flip above, plus dropping `task` from the consumer toolchain list. Neither breaks a `packageManager: "pnpm@…"` install.

---

## Walk-all census

1. Engine isolation already true — strike AC5 — **sharpens-framing**
2. `CONSUMER_TOOLS` hard-requires pnpm — measured — **sharpens-framing**
3. Honor-and-verify is the correct fix; #3784 meets that bar — **sharpens-framing**
4. SLizard P2s — two real-and-fixed, one false positive, quoting repaired — **footnote**
5. No consumer-position demonstration — **sharpens-framing**
6. Scope extras (task drop, getting-started #1909, undeclared default) — **sharpens-framing**
7. Declared-pnpm behavior preserved — **footnote**

No `blocks-the-design` finding. The lean can bind after AC5 is struck and consumer-position proof is named as residual or added.

## Merge line

Do not merge #3784 as written to close all six criteria. Merge the selection, cwd probe, remediation, preflight companion, and Windows quoting repair after AC5 is struck and after a live Corepack cwd probe (or an explicit post-release residual) exists. Leave the getting-started publication-claim rewrite for a different change.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-27T03:45:39Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol-medium
role: critic

Audited PR head: `a59e7d4ce39fb44769261a5fbc6cbf612d60a833`.

Input ceiling: issue comment `5434075404`, inclusive. I fetched issue comment `5434077231` while retrieving the thread, but it is later than the ceiling and I excluded it from the critique. PR body, files, and review comments were separately in the assigned implementation envelope.

## Verdict — SURVIVED, but PR #3784 should not merge as written

The refutation target survives the engine-path challenge: the published consumer path does not need pnpm to execute Deft's TS-backed gates, so the original unconditional pnpm probe is a real false requirement and honoring the repository declaration is the correct design. I nevertheless broke the submitted implementation against acceptance criterion 2: `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` is allowed to override an explicit, conflicting `package.json#packageManager`, so the PR can report a green check for a manager the repository did not declare.

## `audit:engine-need` — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** On current master, consumer mode literally includes both `pnpm --version` and `task --version` in `CONSUMER_TOOLS`, then executes that static list without reading project metadata (`packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:18-25`, `packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:95-106`). But that probe does not describe the actual consumer engine path. `engine:_ts-build` calls the package-manager runner only when `is-buildable-source` is true (`tasks/engine.yml:27-57`). A deposited `.deft/core` is identified as a consumer root (`tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:95-150`), which makes it non-buildable (`tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:153-177`); engine invocation then selects the globally installed `deft`/`directive` CLI rather than a package-manager build (`tasks/engine.yml:76-80`, `tasks/engine.yml:161-168`). Every gate in the consumer composition is CLI-dispatchable (`packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:128-145`, `packages/core/src/check/cli-native-gates.ts:20-33`).

**Failure mode tested.** I tried to establish the triage fork's stronger premise—that removing the pnpm probe would merely defer failure until gate execution—but source tracing gives no consumer-side pnpm invocation on that path. `engine-pm-run.cjs` is a source-build mechanism, not the deposited global-CLI execution mechanism (`tasks/engine-pm-run.cjs:4-10`, `tasks/engine.yml:27-62`).

**Disposition consequence.** AC5 is not a new implementation objective; it is an already-true architectural invariant. Strike it or rewrite it as a regression invariant: “consumer/deposit execution must continue to avoid the source-build `engine:pm-run` path.” Keeping it as a broad feature criterion is what inflates a small validation defect into an engine redesign.

## `audit:implementation` — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The new filesystem resolver returns immediately on any nonblank `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` before it reads `package.json` (`packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.ts:207-220`). It reads `packageManager` only afterward (`packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.ts:222-270`). Tests deliberately lock that order, including a case that says project files must not be read (`packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.test.ts:85-94`, `packages/core/src/resolution/package-manager.test.ts:151-167`). Both the consumer toolchain check and session preflight use that resolver (`packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:217-241`, `packages/core/src/session/toolchain-preflight.ts:228-250`).

I reproduced the consequence on this Windows host against the PR source with real executables: a fixture declaring `pnpm@11.8.0` plus `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=npm` selected npm, ran npm 11.16.0, and returned `exitCode: 0` with source `env-override`. This is a false green: the repository declares pnpm, but the check verifies npm. The inverse conflict selects pnpm in an npm-pinned project and causes Corepack's correct refusal—the original failure class, now conditional on an environment variable.

**Concrete failure mode.** A stale shell/profile/CI `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` disagrees with `packageManager`; Deft either validates the wrong manager or invokes a Corepack shim that correctly refuses the mismatch. Thus PR #3784 does not always “select the declared package manager and verify that manager.”

**Disposition consequence.** Do not merge as written. In the consumer execution resolver, an explicit `packageManager` must be authoritative. A conflicting `DEFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER` should fail clearly as a conflict (or be ignored for this gate); the override may remain a fallback only when the project has no declaration.
